To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the stochastic approximation method can be used to construct a large variety of recursive kernel estimations; (2) the resulting estimators have better properties than Nadaraya's estimators, in the sense that the MWISE of the proposed estimators is smaller than that for Nadaraya's; and (3) we corroborated these theoretical results by simulation studies and a real dataset.
we propose a class of recursive estimators of a density function based on the stochastic approximation method.
the proposed algorithm has a better MSE (Mean Squared Error) than Nadaraya's algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two problems.
a new recursive kernel estimator of a distribution function which has a smaller MWISE than that of Nadaryas estimator.
the problem of estimating the distribution of a random vector from a random sample of the vector, where the random sample is generated by an ergodic Markov chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm has better properties than Nadaraya's algorithm.
the proposed algorithm has a number of advantages over Nadaraya's algorithm.
the proposed estimator is a better choice than the Nadaraya's one in terms of MWISE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithm can provide a good estimator of the distribution function.
the stochastic approximation approach is a promising alternative to the classical kernel approach for the estimation of a distribution.
the proposed estimators are more accurate than Nadaraya's estimators in a large number of situations, especially in the case of small sample sizes and/or when the distribution is multimodal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the estimation of distribution functions, the use of the stochastic approximation method with a stepsize that is a function of the sample size and the kernel bandwidth, is more efficient than the use of Nadaraya-Watson kernel estimator.
the recursive kernel estimator of a distribution function, based on the stochastic approximation algorithm, is more robust to outliers than Nadaraya's kernel estimator.
the recursive kernel estimator can be applied to the estimation of the distribution function, which has been considered a nontrivial problem in the literature.
